1: //! # UNUSED_ENGINE: Unused Constructions Detection Engine
2: //!
3: //! This module implements a file-level rule engine that detects unused variables,
4: //! functions, and dead code in MATLAB source files. It covers 17 distinct check IDs
5: //! that correspond to MATLAB Code Analyzer's "Unused Constructions" category.
6: //!
7: //! ## Checks Implemented
8: //!
9: //! | Check ID | Severity | Description |
10: //! |----------|----------|-------------|
11: //! | NASGU    | Warning  | Variable is assigned but never used |
12: //! | NUSED    | Warning  | Variable is defined (input arg) but never used |
13: //! | NOEFF    | Warning  | Statement has no effect (expression result discarded) |
14: //! | EQEFF    | Warning  | Comparison has no effect (result not used) |
15: //! | ASGLU    | Warning  | Assignment to a variable that is immediately overwritten |
16: //! | SETNU    | Warning  | Output of function assigned but never used |
17: //! | PUSE     | Warning  | Persistent/global variable set but not used |

23: //! | UNRCH    | Warning  | Unreachable code after return/break/continue |

25: //! | VUNUS    | Warning  | Variable assigned in all branches but unused after |
26: //! | MSNU     | Warning  | Struct field set but never read |

644:         // Walk the tree looking for expression nodes at statement level.
645:         walk_for_no_effect(ctx.tree.root_node(), diagnostics, noeff_disabled, eqeff_disabled);
646:     }

648:     /// Run VUNUS check: variable assigned in all branches but unused after.
649:     fn check_vunus(
650:         &self,
651:         table: &SymbolTable,
652:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
653:     ) {
654:         if self.is_check_disabled("VUNUS") {
655:             return;
656:         }
657: 
658:         for scope in &table.scopes {
659:             let output_args: HashSet<&str> = scope
660:                 .defs
661:                 .iter()
662:                 .filter(|d| d.kind == DefKind::OutputArg)
663:                 .map(|d| d.name.as_str())
664:                 .collect();
665: 
666:             // Find variables with multiple defs but no uses.
667:             let mut def_counts: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
668:             for def in &scope.defs {
669:                 if def.kind == DefKind::Assignment {
670:                     *def_counts.entry(def.name.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
671:                 }
672:             }
673: 
674:             for (name, count) in &def_counts {
675:                 if *count < 2 {
676:                     continue;
677:                 }
678:                 if output_args.contains(name) {
679:                     continue;
680:                 }
681:                 if self.should_ignore_name(name) {
682:                     continue;
683:                 }
684:                 if !scope.is_used(name) {
685:                     // Find the last definition for this variable.
686:                     if let Some(last_def) = scope
687:                         .defs
688:                         .iter()
689:                         .rev()
690:                         .find(|d| d.name == *name && d.kind == DefKind::Assignment)
691:                     {
692:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
693:                             rule_id: "VUNUS",
694:                             message: format!(
695:                                 "Variable '{name}' is assigned in multiple branches but never used after"
696:                             ),
697:                             severity: Severity::Warning,
698:                             byte_range: last_def.byte_range.clone(),
699:                             line: last_def.line,
700:                             column: last_def.column,
701:                             fix: None,
702:                         });
703:                     }
704:                 }
705:             }
706:         }
707:     }

709:     /// Run MSNU check: struct field set but never read.
710:     /// This is a heuristic check based on field_expression analysis.
711:     fn check_msnu(
712:         &self,
713:         ctx: &FileContext,
714:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
715:     ) {
716:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNU") {
717:             return;
718:         }
719: 
720:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
721:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
722: 
723:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
724:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
725:             ctx.source,
726:             &mut field_writes,
727:             &mut field_reads,
728:         );
729: 
730:         // Report fields that are written but never read.
731:         for write in &field_writes {
732:             let key = format!("{}.{}", write.object, write.field);
733:             if !field_reads.contains(&key) {
734:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
735:                     rule_id: "MSNU",
736:                     message: format!(
737:                         "Struct field '{}.{}' is set but never read",
738:                         write.object, write.field
739:                     ),
740:                     severity: Severity::Warning,
741:                     byte_range: write.byte_range.clone(),
742:                     line: write.line,
743:                     column: write.column,
744:                     fix: None,
745:                 });
746:             }
747:         }
748:     }
749: 
750:     /// Run MSNE check: struct field doesn't exist (assigned but potential typo).
751:     /// Heuristic: if a struct has many fields and one is only written once with
752:     /// no reads, it may be a typo.
753:     fn check_msne(
754:         &self,
755:         ctx: &FileContext,
756:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
757:     ) {
758:         if self.is_check_disabled("MSNE") {
759:             return;
760:         }
761: 
762:         let mut field_writes: Vec<FieldAccess> = Vec::new();
763:         let mut field_reads: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
764: 
765:         Self::collect_field_accesses(
766:             ctx.tree.root_node(),
767:             ctx.source,
768:             &mut field_writes,
769:             &mut field_reads,
770:         );
771: 
772:         // Group writes by object name.
773:         let mut writes_by_object: HashMap<&str, Vec<&FieldAccess>> = HashMap::new();
774:         for write in &field_writes {
775:             writes_by_object
776:                 .entry(write.object.as_str())
777:                 .or_default()
778:                 .push(write);
779:         }
780: 
781:         // For each object with multiple fields written, check if any field
782:         // is written exactly once and never read — potential typo.
783:         for (object, writes) in &writes_by_object {
784:             if writes.len() < 2 {
785:                 continue;
786:             }
787: 
788:             let mut field_write_count: HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new();
789:             for w in writes {
790:                 *field_write_count.entry(w.field.as_str()).or_insert(0) += 1;
791:             }
792: 
793:             for w in writes {
794:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", object, w.field);
795:                 if field_write_count.get(w.field.as_str()) == Some(&1) && !field_reads.contains(&key)
796:                 {
797:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
798:                         rule_id: "MSNE",
799:                         message: format!(
800:                             "Struct field '{}.{}' is assigned once and never read (possible typo)",
801:                             object, w.field
802:                         ),
803:                         severity: Severity::Info,
804:                         byte_range: w.byte_range.clone(),
805:                         line: w.line,
806:                         column: w.column,
807:                         fix: None,
808:                     });
809:                 }
810:             }
811:         }
812:     }
813: 
814:     /// Collect field accesses (both reads and writes) from the parse tree.
815:     fn collect_field_accesses(
816:         node: Node,
817:         source: &str,
818:         writes: &mut Vec<FieldAccess>,
819:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
820:     ) {
821:         if node.kind() == "assignment" {
822:             // Check if LHS is a field_expression.
823:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
824:                 if lhs.kind() == "field_expression" {
825:                     if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(lhs, source) {
826:                         writes.push(access);
827:                     }
828:                 }
829:             }
830:             // Check RHS for field reads.
831:             if let Some(rhs) = node.child_by_field_name("right") {
832:                 Self::collect_field_reads(rhs, source, reads);
833:             }
834:         } else if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
835:             // A field_expression not on the LHS of assignment is a read.
836:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
837:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
838:                 reads.insert(key);
839:             }
840:         }
841: 
842:         // Recurse into children (skip assignment children we already handled).
843:         if node.kind() != "assignment" {
844:             let count = node.child_count();
845:             for i in 0..count {
846:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
847:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
848:                 }
849:             }
850:         } else {
851:             // For assignments, recurse into children except LHS field_expression.
852:             let count = node.child_count();
853:             for i in 0..count {
854:                 if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
855:                     if child.kind() == "field_expression" {
856:                         if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
857:                             if lhs.id() == child.id() {
858:                                 continue;
859:                             }
860:                         }
861:                     }
862:                     Self::collect_field_accesses(child, source, writes, reads);
863:                 }
864:             }
865:         }
866:     }
867: 
868:     /// Collect field reads from an expression subtree.
869:     fn collect_field_reads(
870:         node: Node,
871:         source: &str,
872:         reads: &mut HashSet<String>,
873:     ) {
874:         if node.kind() == "field_expression" {
875:             if let Some(access) = extract_field_access(node, source) {
876:                 let key = format!("{}.{}", access.object, access.field);
877:                 reads.insert(key);
878:             }
879:         }
880: 
881:         let count = node.child_count();
882:         for i in 0..count {
883:             if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
884:                 Self::collect_field_reads(child, source, reads);
885:             }
886:         }
887:     }
888: }

901:     }

905:     }

908:         // File-level rule — no per-node targeting.
909:         &[]
910:     }

912:     fn has_file_check(&self) -> bool {
913:         true
914:     }

916:     fn check_file(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
917:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
918: 
919:         // 1. Build symbol table.
920:         let table = SymbolTable::build(ctx.tree, ctx.source);
921: 
922:         // 2. Run symbol-based checks.
923:         self.check_nasgu(&table, &mut diagnostics);
924:         self.check_unused_inputs(&table, &mut diagnostics);
925:         self.check_asglu(&table, &mut diagnostics);
926:         self.check_puse(&table, &mut diagnostics);
927:         self.check_setnu(&table, &mut diagnostics);
928:         self.check_preall(&table, &mut diagnostics);
929:         self.check_vanus(&table, &mut diagnostics);
930:         self.check_defnu(&table, &mut diagnostics);
931:         self.check_manu(&table, &mut diagnostics);
932:         self.check_vunus(&table, &mut diagnostics);
933: 
934:         // 3. Run tree-walk checks.
935:         self.check_unrch(ctx, &mut diagnostics);
936:         self.check_noeff_eqeff(ctx, &mut diagnostics);
937:         self.check_msnu(ctx, &mut diagnostics);
938:         self.check_msne(ctx, &mut diagnostics);
939: 
940:         diagnostics
941:     }
942: }

944: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
945: // No-effect statement walker (free function to satisfy clippy)
946: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
947: 
948: /// Recursively walk tree to find statement-level expressions with no effect.
949: fn walk_for_no_effect(
950:     node: Node,
951:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
952:     noeff_disabled: bool,
953:     eqeff_disabled: bool,
954: ) {
955:     // Check if this node is at statement level (parent is block or source_file).
956:     let is_statement_level = node
957:         .parent()
958:         .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
959:         .unwrap_or(false);
960: 
961:     if is_statement_level {
962:         let kind = node.kind();
963: 
964:         // EQEFF: comparison operator at statement level.
965:         if !eqeff_disabled && kind == COMPARISON_NODE {
966:             let pos = node.start_position();
967:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
968:                 rule_id: "EQEFF",
969:                 message: "Comparison has no effect (result is not used)".to_string(),
970:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
971:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
972:                 line: pos.row + 1,
973:                 column: pos.column + 1,
974:                 fix: None,
975:             });
976:         }
977:         // NOEFF: other expression nodes at statement level that are not
978:         // assignments, function_calls, or commands.
979:         else if !noeff_disabled && NO_EFFECT_EXPR_NODES.contains(&kind) {
980:             let pos = node.start_position();
981:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
982:                 rule_id: "NOEFF",
983:                 message: "Statement has no effect (expression result is discarded)"
984:                     .to_string(),
985:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
986:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
987:                 line: pos.row + 1,
988:                 column: pos.column + 1,
989:                 fix: None,
990:             });
991:         }
992:     }
993: 
994:     // Recurse into children.
995:     let count = node.child_count();
996:     for i in 0..count {
997:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
998:             walk_for_no_effect(child, diagnostics, noeff_disabled, eqeff_disabled);
999:         }
1000:     }
1001: }

1007: /// A struct field access (read or write).
1008: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
1009: struct FieldAccess {
1010:     /// The object name (e.g., "s" in "s.field").
1011:     object: String,
1012:     /// The field name (e.g., "field" in "s.field").
1013:     field: String,
1014:     /// Byte range of the full field expression.
1015:     byte_range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
1016:     /// 1-indexed line.
1017:     line: usize,
1018:     /// 1-indexed column.
1019:     column: usize,
1020: }
1021: 
1022: /// Extract a `FieldAccess` from a `field_expression` node.
1023: fn extract_field_access(node: Node, source: &str) -> Option<FieldAccess> {
1024:     // field_expression has an object and a field child.
1025:     let object_node = node.child(0)?;
1026:     let field_node = node.child_by_field_name("field")?;
1027: 
1028:     // Only handle simple identifier objects (not chained field access).
1029:     if object_node.kind() != "identifier" {
1030:         return None;
1031:     }
1032: 
1033:     let object = source[object_node.start_byte()..object_node.end_byte()].to_string();
1034:     let field = source[field_node.start_byte()..field_node.end_byte()].to_string();
1035:     let pos = node.start_position();
1036: 
1037:     Some(FieldAccess {
1038:         object,
1039:         field,
1040:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
1041:         line: pos.row + 1,
1042:         column: pos.column + 1,
1043:     })
1044: }

1046: /// Simple glob pattern matching supporting `*` (any sequence) and `?` (single char).
1047: fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
1048:     let pat: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
1049:     let txt: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
1050:     glob_match_recursive(&pat, &txt, 0, 0)
1051: }
1052: 
1053: /// Recursive glob matching helper.
1054: fn glob_match_recursive(pat: &[char], txt: &[char], pi: usize, ti: usize) -> bool {
1055:     if pi == pat.len() {
1056:         return ti == txt.len();
1057:     }
1058: 
1059:     match pat[pi] {
1060:         '*' => {
1061:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.
1062:             for i in ti..=txt.len() {
1063:                 if glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, i) {
1064:                     return true;
1065:                 }
1066:             }
1067:             false
1068:         }
1069:         '?' => {
1070:             // `?` matches exactly one character.
1071:             if ti < txt.len() {
1072:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
1073:             } else {
1074:                 false
1075:             }
1076:         }
1077:         c => {
1078:             if ti < txt.len() && txt[ti] == c {
1079:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
1080:             } else {
1081:                 false
1082:             }
1083:         }
1084:     }
1085: }

1: //! Shared utilities for rule-module unit tests.
2: //!
3: //! These helpers mirror the `Linter` dispatch so tests can exercise both
4: //! node-level (`check`) and file-level (`check_file`) rules directly,
5: //! without going through the full CLI.
6: //!
7: //! This module is only compiled under `#[cfg(test)]`.
8: 
9: use mlt_core::{Diagnostic, FileContext, NodeContext, Rule};
10: use tree_sitter::{Node, Parser};
11: 
12: /// Parse MATLAB source and return the tree.
13: pub fn parse(source: &str) -> tree_sitter::Tree {
14:     let mut parser = Parser::new();
15:     parser
16:         .set_language(&tree_sitter_matlab::LANGUAGE.into())
17:         .expect("failed to load tree-sitter-matlab");
18:     parser.parse(source, None).expect("parse failed")
19: }
20: 
21: /// Build a `FileContext` with a fixed test file path.
22: pub fn file_ctx<'a>(tree: &'a tree_sitter::Tree, source: &'a str) -> FileContext<'a> {
23:     FileContext {
24:         tree,
25:         source,
26:         file_path: std::path::Path::new("test.m"),
27:     }
28: }
29: 
30: /// Run a rule's node-level `check()` over every node in the tree, mimicking
31: /// the Linter's depth-first dispatch. Returns all diagnostics.
32: pub fn lint_nodes(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
33:     let tree = parse(source);
34:     let path = std::path::Path::new("test.m");
35:     let targets: Vec<&str> = rule.target_node_types().to_vec();
36:     let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
37: 
38:     fn walk(
39:         node: Node,
40:         source: &str,
41:         path: &std::path::Path,
42:         targets: &[&str],
43:         rule: &dyn Rule,
44:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
45:     ) {
46:         if targets.contains(&node.kind()) {
47:             let ctx = NodeContext {
48:                 node,
49:                 source,
50:                 file_path: path,
51:             };
52:             diagnostics.extend(rule.check(&ctx));
53:         }
54:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
55:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
56:             walk(child, source, path, targets, rule, diagnostics);
57:         }
58:     }
59: 
60:     walk(tree.root_node(), source, path, &targets, rule, &mut diagnostics);
61:     diagnostics
62: }
63: 
64: /// Run a rule's file-level `check_file()`. Returns all diagnostics.
65: pub fn lint_file(rule: &dyn Rule, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
66:     let tree = parse(source);
67:     let ctx = file_ctx(&tree, source);
68:     rule.check_file(&ctx)
69: }

71: /// Returns true if any diagnostic has the given rule ID.
72: pub fn has_id(diags: &[Diagnostic], id: &str) -> bool {
73:     diags.iter().any(|d| d.rule_id == id)

311: /// Check if a node is inside a loop.
312: pub(crate) fn is_inside_loop(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
313:     let mut current = node.parent();
314:     while let Some(p) = current {
315:         match p.kind() {
316:             "for_statement" | "while_statement" => return true,
317:             "function_definition" => return false,
318:             _ => {}
319:         }
320:         current = p.parent();
321:     }
322:     false
323: }

325: /// Check if an indexing expression contains `end+1` pattern.
326: pub(crate) fn contains_end_plus_pattern(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str) -> bool {
327:     let text = node_text(node, source);
328:     let normalized: String = text.chars().filter(|c| !c.is_whitespace()).collect();
329:     normalized.contains("end+1")
330: }
331: 
332: /// Check if a matrix literal contains a variable name as an element.
333: pub(crate) fn matrix_contains_var(node: tree_sitter::Node, source: &str, var_name: &str) -> bool {
334:     let count = node.child_count();
335:     for i in 0..count {
336:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
337:             if child.kind() == "identifier" && node_text(child, source) == var_name {
338:                 return true;
339:             }
340:             if child.kind() == "row" && matrix_contains_var(child, source, var_name) {
341:                 return true;
342:             }
343:         }
344:     }
345:     false
346: }
347: 
348: /// Check if a node has a direct child of a specific kind.
349: pub(crate) fn has_child_of_kind(node: &tree_sitter::Node, kind: &str) -> bool {
350:     let count = node.child_count();
351:     for i in 0..count {
352:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
353:             if child.kind() == kind {
354:                 return true;
355:             }
356:         }
357:     }
358:     false
359: }

361: /// Check if the next statement after a node is a for_statement.
362: pub(crate) fn is_followed_by_for(node: tree_sitter::Node) -> bool {
363:     let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
364:     while let Some(sib) = sibling {
365:         match sib.kind() {
366:             "for_statement" => return true,
367:             ";" | "comment" | "line_continuation" => {
368:                 sibling = sib.next_sibling();
369:             }
370:             _ => return false,
371:         }
372:     }
373:     false
374: }

```python
def extract_block(text, start, open_brace):
    """Given start index at/after which the first '{' appears, return end index
    just past the matching '}'. Assumes braces balanced."""
    i = text.index(open_brace, start)
    depth = 0
    while i < len(text):

        if c == '{':
            depth += 1
        elif c == '}':
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return i + 1
        i += 1
    raise ValueError("unbalanced")
```

```python
def extract_anchored(marker_regex):
    """Find line matching marker_regex; walk back over /// doc lines; then
    from the marker line's first '{' brace-match; return the full text
    (doc + item through closing brace) and the end offset."""
    m = re.search(marker_regex, text, re.M)
    if not m: raise SystemExit("anchor not found: " + marker_regex)
    # line start
    line_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, m.start()) + 1
    # walk back over doc comment lines
    start = line_start
    while start > 0:
        prev_end = start - 1  # index of '\n' before the line
        prev_start = text.rfind("\n", 0, prev_end) + 1
        prev_line = text[prev_start:prev_end]
        if re.match(r"^\s*///", prev_line):
            start = prev_start
        else:
            break
    end = match_braces(text, m.start())
    return text[start:end], end
```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""PURE MECHANICAL REFACTOR: split crates/mlt_rules/src/unused.rs into
crates/mlt_rules/src/unused/ (one file per independent check).

- Never writes to unused.rs (only reads it).
- Only creates files under crates/mlt_rules/src/unused/.
- Method/test bodies are copied byte-for-byte from the original; the only
  systematic edits are `pub(crate) ` visibility prefixes on moved methods,
  free helpers, and consts (exactly per the approved plan).
"""

import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = "/home/watermarkhu/repositories/mlt"
ORIG = os.path.join(ROOT, "crates/mlt_rules/src/unused.rs")
OUTDIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "crates/mlt_rules/src/unused")

text = open(ORIG, encoding="utf-8").read()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Low-level extraction helpers (all operate on the ORIGINAL text)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def line_end(match):
    """Index just past the newline ending the line containing `match`."""
    nl = text.find("\n", match.start())
    return nl + 1 if nl != -1 else len(text)


def find_line_start(pos):
    """Index of the start of the line containing `pos`."""
    return text.rfind("\n", 0, pos) + 1


def match_braces(pos):
    """From the first '{' at/after `pos`, return index just past the matching '}'.
    Assumes braces in the source are balanced."""
    i = text.index("{", pos)
    depth = 0
    while i < len(text):
        c = text[i]
        if c == "{":
            depth += 1
        elif c == "}":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0:
                return i + 1
        i += 1
    raise SystemExit(f"unbalanced braces from offset {pos}")


def extract_anchored(marker_regex):
    """Extract a doc-commented item whose definition line matches `marker_regex`.

    Walks back over consecutive `///` lines, then forward to the matching
    closing brace of the first '{' in the definition line. Returns
    (block_text, end_offset).
    """
    m = re.search(marker_regex, text, re.M)
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"anchor not found: {marker_regex!r}")
    start = find_line_start(m.start())
    # walk back over doc-comment lines
    while start > 0:
        prev_end = start - 1
        prev_start = find_line_start(prev_end)
        prev_line = text[prev_start:prev_end]
        if re.match(r"^\s*///", prev_line):
            start = prev_start
        else:
            break
    end = match_braces(m.start())
    return text[start:end], end


def extract_method(name, indent):
    return extract_anchored(r"^" + re.escape(indent) + r"fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(")


def extract_test(name):
    """Extract a `#[test] fn NAME(...) { ... }` block (kept verbatim)."""
    m = re.search(
        r"^    #\[test\]\n    fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(",
        text,
        re.M,
    )
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"test not found: {name!r}")
    start = find_line_start(m.start())
    end = match_braces(m.start())
    return text[start:end]


def section_comment(regex):
    """Extract the full `// -- ...` comment line matching `regex` (no newline)."""
    m = re.search(regex, text, re.M)
    if not m:
        raise SystemExit(f"section comment not found: {regex!r}")
    return m.group(0)


def pubcrate(text_block, regex):
    """Insert `pub(crate) ` before every line matching `regex`."""
    return re.sub(regex, r"pub(crate) \1", text_block, flags=re.M)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Data: what moves where
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# check method name -> target module file
MOVED_METHODS = {
    "check_nasgu": "check_nasgu",
    "check_unused_inputs": "check_unused_inputs",
    "check_asglu": "check_asglu",
    "check_puse": "check_puse",
    "check_setnu": "check_setnu",
    "check_preall": "check_preall",
    "check_vanus": "check_vanus",
    "check_defnu": "check_defnu",
    "check_manu": "check_manu",
    "check_unrch": "check_unrch",
    "check_noeff_eqeff": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    "check_vunus": "check_vunus",
}
# `walk_for_no_effect` (free walker) must stay with its only caller.
WALKER_FILE = "check_noeff_eqeff"

CHECK_MODULES = sorted(set(MOVED_METHODS.values()))

# test fn name -> target module file
MOVED_TESTS = {
    "nasgu_fires_on_unused_assignment": "check_nasgu",
    "nasgu_ok_when_used": "check_nasgu",
    "nused_fires_on_unused_input": "check_unused_inputs",
    "nused_ok_when_input_used": "check_unused_inputs",
    "inusa_fires_on_unused_input": "check_unused_inputs",
    "inusa_ok_when_input_used": "check_unused_inputs",
    "inusd_fires_on_unused_input": "check_unused_inputs",
    "inusd_ok_when_input_used": "check_unused_inputs",
    "noeff_fires_on_discarded_expression": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    "noeff_ok_on_assignment": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    "eqeff_fires_on_discarded_comparison": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    "eqeff_ok_when_result_used": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    "asglu_fires_on_overwritten_assignment": "check_asglu",
    "asglu_ok_when_used_between": "check_asglu",
    "setnu_fires_when_nasgu_disabled": "check_setnu",
    "setnu_ok_when_nasgu_enabled": "check_setnu",
    "puse_fires_on_unused_global": "check_puse",
    "puse_ok_when_global_used": "check_puse",
    "preall_fires_on_unused_loop_var": "check_preall",
    "preall_ok_when_loop_var_used": "check_preall",
    "vanus_fires_on_unused_ans_assignment": "check_vanus",
    "vanus_ok_when_ans_used": "check_vanus",
    "defnu_fires_on_uncalled_local_function": "check_defnu",
    "defnu_ok_when_local_function_called": "check_defnu",
    "unrch_fires_after_return": "check_unrch",
    "unrch_ok_without_terminator": "check_unrch",
    "vunus_fires_on_branch_assignment_unused": "check_vunus",
    "vunus_ok_when_used_after_branches": "check_vunus",
    "manu_fires_on_uncalled_method": "check_manu",
    "manu_ok_when_method_called": "check_manu",
}
# tests that stay in mod.rs (checks sharing mutable field-access traversal state)
KEPT_TESTS = [
    "msnu_fires_on_field_never_read",
    "msnu_ok_when_field_read",
    "msne_fires_on_typo_field",
    "msne_ok_when_all_fields_read",
]

# section comment regex -> target file
SECTION_COMMENTS = {
    r"^    // -- NASGU:.*": "check_nasgu",
    r"^    // -- NUSED / INUSA / INUSD:.*": "check_unused_inputs",
    r"^    // -- NOEFF:.*": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    r"^    // -- EQEFF:.*": "check_noeff_eqeff",
    r"^    // -- ASGLU:.*": "check_asglu",
    r"^    // -- SETNU:.*": "check_setnu",
    r"^    // -- PUSE:.*": "check_puse",
    r"^    // -- PREALL:.*": "check_preall",
    r"^    // -- VANUS:.*": "check_vanus",
    r"^    // -- DEFNU:.*": "check_defnu",
    r"^    // -- UNRCH:.*": "check_unrch",
    r"^    // -- VUNUS:.*": "check_vunus",
    r"^    // -- MANU:.*": "check_manu",
    r"^    // -- MSNU:.*": "mod.rs",
    r"^    // -- MSNE:.*": "mod.rs",
}

# one-line `//!` module docs for each check file
CHECK_DOCS = {
    "check_nasgu": "NASGU check: variable is assigned but never used.",
    "check_unused_inputs": "NUSED/INUSA/INUSD checks: input arguments that are never used.",
    "check_asglu": "ASGLU check: value assigned to a variable that is immediately overwritten.",
    "check_puse": "PUSE check: global/persistent variable declared but never used.",
    "check_setnu": "SETNU check: output of a function assigned but never used.",
    "check_preall": "PREALL check: loop variable preallocated but unused.",
    "check_vanus": "VANUS check: value assigned to `ans` is unused.",
    "check_defnu": "DEFNU check: local function defined but never called.",
    "check_manu": "MANU check: method defined but never called.",
    "check_unrch": "UNRCH check: unreachable code after return/break/continue.",
    "check_noeff_eqeff": "NOEFF/EQEFF checks: statements with no effect.",
    "check_vunus": "VUNUS check: variable assigned in all branches but unused after.",
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Pre-extract the pieces we need from the original
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

doc_text = text[: re.search(r"^use std::collections", text, re.M).start()]

uses_start = re.search(r"^use std::collections", text, re.M).start()
uses_end = line_end(re.search(r"^use crate::analysis::symbols", text, re.M))
uses_text = text[uses_start:uses_end]

config_start = re.search(r"^// Rule-specific configuration", text, re.M).start()
config_end = match_braces(re.search(r"^pub struct UnusedConfig \{", text, re.M).start())
config_text = text[config_start:config_end]

consts_start = re.search(r"^// Constants", text, re.M).start()
consts_end = re.search(r"^// Rule implementation", text, re.M).start()
consts_text = text[consts_start:consts_end]

# impl head: `impl UnusedEngine {` through the closing `}` of should_ignore_name
impl_start = re.search(r"^impl UnusedEngine \{", text, re.M).start()
_, should_ignore_end = extract_method("should_ignore_name", "    ")
impl_head = text[impl_start:should_ignore_end]

# kept methods (share the mutable field-access traversal state)
kept_msnu, _ = extract_method("check_msnu", "    ")
kept_msne, _ = extract_method("check_msne", "    ")
kept_collect_acc, _ = extract_method("collect_field_accesses", "    ")
kept_collect_reads, _ = extract_method("collect_field_reads", "    ")

rule_trait, _ = extract_anchored(r"^impl Rule for UnusedEngine \{")

helpers_start = re.search(r"^// Helper types and functions", text, re.M).start()
_, glob_end = extract_method("glob_match_recursive", "")
helpers_text = text[helpers_start:glob_end]
helpers_text = pubcrate(helpers_text, r"^(struct FieldAccess \{)")
helpers_text = pubcrate(helpers_text, r"^(fn (?:extract_field_access|matches_simple_glob|glob_match_recursive)\()")

autoreg_start = re.search(r"^// Auto-registration", text, re.M).start()
autoreg_end = line_end(re.search(r"^\)\);", text, re.M))
autoreg_text = text[autoreg_start:autoreg_end]

tests_start = re.search(r"^// Tests", text, re.M).start()
_, engine_with_end = extract_method("engine_with", "    ")
tests_prologue = text[tests_start:engine_with_end]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assemble mod.rs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

mod_rs = []
mod_rs.append(doc_text)                       # module //! doc (verbatim)
mod_rs.append(uses_text)                      # all use statements (verbatim)
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append("// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
mod_rs.append("// Submodules: one file per independent check\n")
mod_rs.append("// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
for name in CHECK_MODULES:
    mod_rs.append(f"mod {name};\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(config_text)
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append(consts_text.rstrip() + "\n")    # consts -> pub(crate)
mod_rs = mod_rs[:-1]
mod_rs.append(pubcrate(mod_rs.pop(), r"^(const )"))
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append("// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
mod_rs.append("// Rule implementation\n")
mod_rs.append("// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(extract_anchored(r"^pub struct UnusedEngine \{")[0])
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append(impl_head)
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(kept_msnu)
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(kept_msne)
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(kept_collect_acc)
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(kept_collect_reads)
mod_rs.append("\n}\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(rule_trait)
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append(helpers_text)
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append(autoreg_text)
mod_rs.append("\n\n")
mod_rs.append(tests_prologue)
mod_rs.append("\n")
# kept tests (MSNU/MSNE) with their section comments
msnu_comment = section_comment(r"^    // -- MSNU:.*")
msne_comment = section_comment(r"^    // -- MSNE:.*")
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(msnu_comment + "\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
for t in KEPT_TESTS[:2]:
    mod_rs.append(extract_test(t))
    mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append(msne_comment + "\n")
mod_rs.append("\n")
for t in KEPT_TESTS[2:]:
    mod_rs.append(extract_test(t))
    mod_rs.append("\n")
mod_rs.append("}\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Assemble the per-check files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def build_check_file(module, doc_line, methods, tests_with_comments):
    out = []
    out.append(f"//! {doc_line}\n")
    out.append("\n")
    out.append("use super::*;\n")
    out.append("\n")
    out.append("impl UnusedEngine {\n")
    for method_text in methods:
        out.append(method_text)
        out.append("\n")
    out.append("}\n")
    out.append("\n")
    out.append("#[cfg(test)]\n")
    out.append("mod tests {\n")
    out.append("    use super::*;\n")
    out.append("    use crate::test_util::{has_id, lint_file};\n")
    out.append("    use mlt_core::Config;\n")
    out.append("\n")
    out.append("    fn engine() -> Box<dyn Rule> {\n")
    out.append("        UnusedEngine::from_config(&Config::default())\n")
    out.append("    }\n")
    if module == "check_setnu":
        out.append("\n")
        engine_with_block, _ = extract_method("engine_with", "    ")
        out.append(engine_with_block)
    out.append("\n")
    for comment, tests in tests_with_comments:
        out.append(comment + "\n")
        out.append("\n")
        for t in tests:
            out.append(t)
            out.append("\n")
    out.append("}\n")
    return "".join(out)


def module_tests(module):
    """Ordered (section_comment, [test_block, ...]) pairs for a module."""
    tests = [name for name, mod in MOVED_TESTS.items() if mod == module]
    # group by consecutive section comments in original order
    groups = []
    current = None
    for name in tests:
        m = re.search(r"^    #\[test\]\n    fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(", text, re.M)
        # find the nearest preceding section comment belonging to this module
        prefix = text[: m.start()]
        comment = None
        for idx, line in enumerate(prefix.splitlines()):
            if re.match(r"^    // -- ", line):
                for rxs, target in SECTION_COMMENTS.items():
                    if re.match(rxs, line) and target == module:
                        comment = line
        if comment is not None and (current is None or current[0] != comment):
            current = (comment, [])
            groups.append(current)
        current[1].append(extract_test(name))
    return groups


files = {}
for module in CHECK_MODULES:
    methods = []
    for name, mod in MOVED_METHODS.items():
        if mod == module:
            block, _ = extract_method(name, "    ")
            # add pub(crate) visibility (required for dispatch from mod.rs)
            block = re.sub(r"^    fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(",
                           r"    pub(crate) fn " + name + r"(", block, count=1)
            methods.append(block)
    if module == WALKER_FILE:
        walker, _ = extract_method("walk_for_no_effect", "")
        walker = walker.replace("fn walk_for_no_effect(",
                                "pub(crate) fn walk_for_no_effect(", 1)
        methods.append(walker)
    tests_with_comments = module_tests(module)
    files[module] = build_check_file(module, CHECK_DOCS[module], methods,
                                     tests_with_comments)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Write files
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

os.makedirs(OUTDIR, exist_ok=True)
written = {}
written["mod.rs"] = "".join(mod_rs)
for module, content in files.items():
    written[module + ".rs"] = content

for fname, content in written.items():
    path = os.path.join(OUTDIR, fname)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(content)
    print(f"wrote {path} ({len(content.splitlines())} lines)")

print("\nDone.")

11:     ) {
12:         let noeff_disabled = self.is_check_disabled("NOEFF");
13:         let eqeff_disabled = self.is_check_disabled("EQEFF");

15:         if noeff_disabled && eqeff_disabled {

17:         }
18: 
19:         // Walk the tree looking for expression nodes at statement level.

21:     }
22: /// Recursively walk tree to find statement-level expressions with no effect.
23: pub(crate) fn walk_for_no_effect(
24:     node: Node,
25:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
26:     noeff_disabled: bool,
27:     eqeff_disabled: bool,
28: ) {
29:     // Check if this node is at statement level (parent is block or source_file).
30:     let is_statement_level = node
31:         .parent()
32:         .map(|p| STATEMENT_PARENTS.contains(&p.kind()))
33:         .unwrap_or(false);
34: 
35:     if is_statement_level {
36:         let kind = node.kind();
37: 
38:         // EQEFF: comparison operator at statement level.
39:         if !eqeff_disabled && kind == COMPARISON_NODE {
40:             let pos = node.start_position();
41:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
42:                 rule_id: "EQEFF",
43:                 message: "Comparison has no effect (result is not used)".to_string(),
44:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
45:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
46:                 line: pos.row + 1,
47:                 column: pos.column + 1,
48:                 fix: None,
49:             });
50:         }
51:         // NOEFF: other expression nodes at statement level that are not
52:         // assignments, function_calls, or commands.
53:         else if !noeff_disabled && NO_EFFECT_EXPR_NODES.contains(&kind) {
54:             let pos = node.start_position();
55:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
56:                 rule_id: "NOEFF",
57:                 message: "Statement has no effect (expression result is discarded)"
58:                     .to_string(),
59:                 severity: Severity::Warning,
60:                 byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
61:                 line: pos.row + 1,
62:                 column: pos.column + 1,
63:                 fix: None,
64:             });
65:         }
66:     }
67: 
68:     // Recurse into children.
69:     let count = node.child_count();
70:     for i in 0..count {
71:         if let Some(child) = node.child(i) {
72:             walk_for_no_effect(child, diagnostics, noeff_disabled, eqeff_disabled);

3: //! This module implements a file-level rule engine that detects unused variables,

5: //! that correspond to MATLAB Code Analyzer's "Unused Constructions" category.

7: //! ## Checks Implemented

9: //! | Check ID | Severity | Description |
10: //! |----------|----------|-------------|
11: //! | NASGU    | Warning  | Variable is assigned but never used |
12: //! | NUSED    | Warning  | Variable is defined (input arg) but never used |
13: //! | NOEFF    | Warning  | Statement has no effect (expression result discarded) |
14: //! | EQEFF    | Warning  | Comparison has no effect (result not used) |
15: //! | ASGLU    | Warning  | Assignment to a variable that is immediately overwritten |
16: //! | SETNU    | Warning  | Output of function assigned but never used |
17: //! | PUSE     | Warning  | Persistent/global variable set but not used |

418:     let field_node = node.child_by_field_name("field")?;

438: /// Simple glob pattern matching supporting `*` (any sequence) and `?` (single char).
439: pub(crate) fn matches_simple_glob(pattern: &str, text: &str) -> bool {
440:     let pat: Vec<char> = pattern.chars().collect();
441:     let txt: Vec<char> = text.chars().collect();
442:     glob_match_recursive(&pat, &txt, 0, 0)
443: }
444: 
445: /// Recursive glob matching helper.
446: pub(crate) fn glob_match_recursive(pat: &[char], txt: &[char], pi: usize, ti: usize) -> bool {
447:     if pi == pat.len() {
448:         return ti == txt.len();
449:     }
450: 
451:     match pat[pi] {
452:         '*' => {
453:             // `*` matches zero or more characters.
454:             for i in ti..=txt.len() {
455:                 if glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, i) {
456:                     return true;
457:                 }
458:             }
459:             false
460:         }
461:         '?' => {
462:             // `?` matches exactly one character.
463:             if ti < txt.len() {
464:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
465:             } else {
466:                 false
467:             }
468:         }
469:         c => {
470:             if ti < txt.len() && txt[ti] == c {
471:                 glob_match_recursive(pat, txt, pi + 1, ti + 1)
472:             } else {
473:                 false
474:             }
475:         }
476:     }
477: }

orig_fn_re = {name: r"^    fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(" for name in MOVED_METHODS}
orig_fn_re[WALKER] = r"^fn " + re.escape(WALKER) + r"\("

print("== 1. moved method / walker bodies vs original ==")
for name, module in sorted(MOVED_METHODS.items()):
    orig_block, ok1 = find_block(orig, orig_fn_re[name])
    new_block, ok2 = find_block(read_new(module + ".rs"),
                                r"^    pub\(crate\) fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(")
    if not ok1 or not ok2:
        failures.append(f"{name}: extraction failed (orig={ok1} new={ok2})")
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: extraction failed (orig={ok1}, new={ok2})")
        continue
    o, n = normalize(orig_block), normalize(new_block)
    if o == n:
        print(f"  OK   {name} -> {module}.rs  ({len(o)} normalized lines)")
    else:
        failures.append(f"{name}: body differs")
        print(f"  FAIL {name}: body differs")
        for a, b in zip(o, n):
            if a != b:
                print(f"    orig: {a!r}")
                print(f"    new : {b!r}")
        if len(o) != len(n):
            print(f"    (orig {len(o)} lines, new {len(n)} lines)")

walker_orig, ok1 = find_block(orig, r"^fn " + re.escape(WALKER) + r"\(")
walker_new, ok2 = find_block(read_new(WALKER_FILE + ".rs"),
                             r"^pub\(crate\) fn " + re.escape(WALKER) + r"\(")
if ok1 and ok2 and normalize(walker_orig) == normalize(walker_new):
    print(f"  OK   {WALKER} -> {WALKER_FILE}.rs (walker with its check)")
else:
    failures.append(f"{WALKER}: body differs")
    print(f"  FAIL {WALKER}: body differs")

# walker must NOT appear in mod.rs or any other check file
for fname in new_files():
    content = read_new(fname)
    hits = len(re.findall(r"fn " + re.escape(WALKER) + r"\(", content))
    expect = 1 if fname == WALKER_FILE + ".rs" else 0
    if hits != expect:
        failures.append(f"{WALKER} appears {hits}x in {fname} (expected {expect})")
        print(f"  FAIL walker presence in {fname}: {hits} (expected {expect})")

# each moved method appears exactly once across unused/
print("== 1b. moved method presence (exactly once each) ==")
for name, module in sorted(MOVED_METHODS.items()):
    total = 0
    for fname in new_files():
        content = read_new(fname)
        total += len(re.findall(r"fn " + re.escape(name) + r"\(", content))
    if total == 1:
        print(f"  OK   {name} appears once (in {module}.rs)")
    else:
        failures.append(f"{name} appears {total}x across unused/ (expected 1)")
        print(f"  FAIL {name} appears {total}x across unused/ (expected 1)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. every check ID appears exactly once across unused/
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("== 2. check IDs appear exactly once across unused/ ==")
counts = {cid: 0 for cid in CHECK_IDS}
unknown = []
for fname in new_files():
    content = read_new(fname)
    for m in re.finditer(r'rule_id:\s*"([A-Z0-9_]+)"', content):
        if m.group(1) in counts:
            counts[m.group(1)] += 1
        else:
            unknown.append((m.group(1), fname))
for cid in CHECK_IDS:
    if counts[cid] == 1:
        print(f"  OK   {cid}: exactly once")
    else:
        failures.append(f"{cid}: appears {counts[cid]}x (expected 1)")
        print(f"  FAIL {cid}: appears {counts[cid]}x (expected 1)")
if unknown:
    failures.append(f"unknown rule_ids in code: {unknown}")
    print(f"  FAIL unknown rule_id values: {unknown}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. dispatch calls match
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("== 3. check_file dispatch calls match ==")
m_orig = re.search(r"fn check_file\(&self, ctx: &FileContext\) -> Vec<Diagnostic> \{.*?\n    \}\n\}",
                   orig, re.S)
m_new = re.search(r"fn check_file\(&self, ctx: &FileContext\) -> Vec<Diagnostic> \{.*?\n    \}\n\}",
                  read_new("mod.rs"), re.S)
if not m_orig or not m_new:
    failures.append("could not locate check_file in original or mod.rs")
    print("  FAIL could not locate check_file")
else:
    calls_orig = extract_calls(m_orig.group(0))
    calls_new = extract_calls(m_new.group(0))
    if calls_orig == calls_new:
        print(f"  OK   {len(calls_orig)} dispatch calls match in order: {calls_orig}")
    else:
        failures.append(f"dispatch mismatch: {calls_orig} vs {calls_new}")
        print(f"  FAIL orig: {calls_orig}")
        print(f"       new : {calls_new}")

# every dispatched check method must be defined somewhere in unused/
all_method_defs = set()
for fname in new_files():
    all_method_defs.update(re.findall(r"fn (check_\w+)\(", read_new(fname)))
for call in set(calls_orig if 'calls_orig' in dir() else []):
    if call not in all_method_defs:
        failures.append(f"dispatch calls undefined method {call}")
        print(f"  FAIL dispatch calls undefined method {call}")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. moved-test count + bodies match
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("== 4. moved-test count + bodies match ==")
orig_test_count = len(re.findall(r"^    #\[test\]", orig, re.M))
new_test_count = sum(len(re.findall(r"^    #\[test\]", read_new(f), re.M))
                     for f in new_files())
print(f"  #[test] count: original={orig_test_count}, new total={new_test_count}")
if orig_test_count != new_test_count:
    failures.append(f"test count mismatch: {orig_test_count} vs {new_test_count}")

for name, module in sorted(MOVED_TESTS.items()):
    orig_block, ok1 = find_test(orig, name)
    new_block, ok2 = find_test(read_new(module + ".rs"), name)
    if not ok1 or not ok2:
        failures.append(f"test {name}: extraction failed (orig={ok1} new={ok2})")
        print(f"  FAIL test {name}: extraction failed")
        continue
    if normalize(orig_block, strip_pubcrate=False) == normalize(new_block, strip_pubcrate=False):
        print(f"  OK   {name} -> {module}.rs")
    else:
        failures.append(f"test {name}: body differs")
        print(f"  FAIL test {name}: body differs")

# kept tests must still be in mod.rs and identical
mod_rs_content = read_new("mod.rs")
for name in KEPT_TESTS:
    orig_block, ok1 = find_test(orig, name)
    new_block, ok2 = find_test(mod_rs_content, name)
    if ok1 and ok2 and normalize(orig_block, strip_pubcrate=False) == normalize(new_block, strip_pubcrate=False):
        print(f"  OK   {name} kept in mod.rs (unchanged)")
    else:
        failures.append(f"kept test {name}: missing or differs in mod.rs")
        print(f"  FAIL kept test {name}: missing or differs in mod.rs")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. original unused.rs unchanged vs git HEAD
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("== 5. original unused.rs unchanged vs git HEAD ==")
head = subprocess.run(["git", "show", "HEAD:crates/mlt_rules/src/unused.rs"],
                      cwd=ROOT, capture_output=True, text=True)
if head.returncode == 0 and head.stdout == orig:
    print("  OK   unused.rs identical to git HEAD")
else:
    failures.append("unused.rs differs from git HEAD")
    print("  FAIL unused.rs differs from git HEAD")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. nothing created/modified outside unused/
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print("== 6. git status: only unused/ touched ==")
status = subprocess.run(["git", "status", "--porcelain"], cwd=ROOT,
                        capture_output=True, text=True).stdout
bad = []
for line in status.splitlines():
    path = line[3:].strip('"')
    if not (path.startswith("crates/mlt_rules/src/unused/")
            or path == "crates/mlt_rules/src/unused"):
        bad.append(line)
if bad:
    failures.append(f"changes outside unused/: {bad}")
    print("  FAIL unexpected changes:")
    for b in bad:
        print(f"    {b}")
else:
    print("  OK   only unused/ files are new (untracked)")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# summary
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print()
if failures:
    print(f"VERIFICATION FAILED: {len(failures)} issue(s)")
    for f in failures:
        print(f"  - {f}")
    sys.exit(1)
print("VERIFICATION PASSED: all checks green.")
